title: Move baked cookies from a sheet pan to a cooling rack with a turner, without touching or breaking them
instruction: Move the four cookies from the sheet pan onto the cooling rack with the spatula, without touching or breaking them, then put the spatula back on its rest.
context: Lifting freshly baked cookies off a sheet pan onto a cooling rack with a spatula is one of the most familiar moments in a home kitchen, a school bake sale or a bakery; cookie-dough packages end their directions with it (cool briefly on the sheet, then remove). Anyone can judge the result at a glance: every cookie whole and flat on the rack, none broken, dropped or touched by hand. Nothing is turned over: the skill is getting a 0.6 mm blade under a brittle item, carrying it level, and setting it down on wire without a drop, for several items in a row, with no hand ever on the food.
setup: On the table, as in the screenshot (x forward from the robot, y to its left, from the midpoint between the arm bases; arms at y +0.305 and -0.305 m). (1) Aluminium quarter sheet pan, 330 x 241 mm rim, 305 x 216 mm flat floor, 25 mm deep, about 0.40 kg, bare (no liner), long side pointing away from the robot, centre at x 0.335, y -0.060; loose on the table. (2) Four baked cookies from Otis Spunkmeyer Sweet Discovery Triple Chocolate frozen cookie dough (item 58814, 38 g pucks; the maker's specification gives the baked cookie as 72 to 82 mm across, target 77 mm, and 35 g), simulated as 76 mm across, 10 mm thick and 35 g, firm and brittle, flat side down on the far two thirds of the pan with centres at (0.335, -0.115), (0.335, -0.005), (0.440, -0.115) and (0.440, -0.005). (3) Wire cooling rack, 305 x 216 mm, 17 mm high, 2 mm wires 10 mm apart running away from the robot, about 0.22 kg, loose, right of the pan with centre at x 0.360, y -0.330. (4) Offset turner (cookie spatula): stainless blade 90 x 65 mm, 0.6 mm thick, 30 mm below a 110 x 22 x 14 mm plastic handle, about 69 g, lying on a rest fixed to the table (two posts 32 mm high under the handle, a pad under the blade) with the handle's middle at x 0.280, y -0.600, blade pointing away from the robot. Both arms start raised in the ready pose.
scoring: Count at the end, from a photo plus the trial video. Each cookie is one of: GOOD (+0.2): lying flat (within 8 degrees) with its whole outline on the rack's wires, not on another cookie or on the turner, at rest, in one piece, never touched by a gripper or any other part of the robot, and never dropped. SPOILED (-0.1): broken into two or more pieces at any time; or touched by any part of the robot at any time; or dropped (a free fall of about 18 mm or more, 0.6 m/s downward in simulation); or ending anywhere other than the pan or the rack (table, floor, turner, hanging on a rim). LEFT (0): still on the pan in one piece and untouched, or on the rack but overhanging its frame, leaning or stacked. Score = 0.2 x GOOD - 0.1 x SPOILED, never below 0, so four good cookies give 0.8. The last 0.2 is given only when all four are GOOD and, for at least 1 second, the pan is where it started (centre within 30 mm, turned no more than 10 degrees, flat on the table), the turner is back on its rest (handle middle within 15 mm of its starting place, pointing within 15 degrees, lying on the posts), both grippers are at least 80 mm from the pan, the rack and the turner, and nothing is moving. The whole trial scores 0 if the pan is ever tipped more than 10 degrees or lifted more than 20 mm off the table (a hot pan must not be poured from). Doing nothing scores 0. Measure with a ruler against tape marks made at setup (pan outline, rest), a count of whole and broken cookies, and the video for touches and drops.
reset_notes: Cookies: bake the frozen pucks on a parchment-lined tray at the maker's setting (convection oven 300 F, 11 to 14 minutes), cool them on the tray at room temperature for 20 minutes until firm, and accept only cookies 72 to 82 mm across (ruler, mean of two perpendicular diameters), 31 to 39 g (kitchen scale), whole and flat; then set four on the bare trial pan at the marked places with a spatula. Replace any broken or touched cookie with an accepted one. Put the pan and rack back on their tape marks and the turner on its rest, blade away from the robot.
fidelity: True-size rigid bodies in PhysX with real contact; the 0.6 mm blade is a collider. A cookie is one rigid body that breaks by a criterion on measured contact forces (0.02 N m bending, 3 N squeeze, 10 N press); it cannot crumble or bend. Its base edge curls up 1.5 mm, which lets the blade in. Friction is fixed (cookie on pan 0.7, on blade 0.25); cookies do not stick, the pan is not hot, the blade does not flex. With a light touch the pan stays put, so one arm does the job.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; scripted demo: 1.0 (two runs, 35 g cookies)
